title: Export audio

hints.format: WAV/AIFF/FLAC are lossless; MP3/OGG are lossy and much smaller.
hints.sampleRate: Samples per second. Lower rates make smaller files but remove high frequencies (max frequency = rate / 2).
hints.channels: Source keeps the project channels. Mono halves the size and is ideal for 3D/positional SFX.
hints.bitDepth: 16-bit is CD quality and enough for games; 24-bit for masters and further editing.
hints.dither: Adds very low noise when reducing bit depth to avoid quantization distortion on quiet sounds.
hints.bitrateMode: CBR: constant bitrate (predictable size). VBR: quality-based, usually smaller for the same quality.
hints.bitrate: Higher bitrate = better quality and bigger file. 128–192 kbps is good for music, 64 kbps for voice.
hints.resampleQuality: Quality of the sample-rate conversion. Best is slower but cleanest.
hints.fileName: Only a suggestion: you choose the final folder and name in the save dialog.
hints.askLocation: You will choose where to save before anything is written.
hints.oggAbr: OGG Vorbis uses an average bitrate (ABR) in this mode.

formatHint.ogg: Lossy Vorbis, great for games (Unity, Godot, Unreal).

sampleRate.keepHint: Use the project sample rate (highest among the tracks).
